messages.subject: Help with errors running right-censored and right-and-left-censored poisson models
parts:
I am trying to fit poisson models to data describing how long people wait to get their driver's license. I was hoping to run at least a few different model specifications, to see if my parameter estimates are robust/consistent across choices of likelihood function. 

The right-censored poisson includes individuals who have not yet received a driver's license, and therefore are right-censored above their current age. In this model, the dependent count variable is how many years past 16 a person waits to get their driver's license (I'm looking at the US context, where 16 is the normal licensing age), so many people are at 0 (i.e. they got their license when they were 16). 

The right-and-left-censored poisson has the same right-censoring as before, but I've rescaled the dependent count variable to be on the year/age scale. In this model, I am considering anyone who received their driver's license at age 16 to potentially be left-censored. In other words, this model considers that these eager individuals might have gotten their license earlier if they weren't constrained by licensing age laws, with the thought that this model specification might better capture the "true" relationships between predictor variables and the dependent variable.

Both types of models have been giving me similar error messages, but I'll give you an example for the right-and-left-censored poisson.

Here's the error message I get:

SAMPLING FOR MODEL '77e33b928f7fb5717a908d32279f49a7' NOW (CHAIN 1).
[1] "Rejecting initial value:"                                      
[2] "  Log probability evaluates to log(0), i.e. negative infinity."
[3] "  Stan can't start sampling from this initial value."          
[4] "Error : "
error occurred during calling the sampler; sampling not done  

Below is my code in rstan. The error seems to go away when I use fewer predictor variables, so I'm sharing the model with the fewest parameters that still creates the error - as you can see, it is still quite long (apologies!). The error goes away entirely when I only include run the model on the uncensored cases, which is reassuring but still not terribly helpful.
